To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multifragmentation of hot nuclei formed in central collisions of heavy ions is a signature of liquid-gas phase transition, which can be studied by means of a correlation between dynamical (fragment size distribution) and thermodynamical (temperature) observables.

the multifragmentation of hot nuclei is a liquid-gas phase transition; this transition is characterized by a first order phase transition line and a critical point; the transition line is crossed at a temperature of 5.5 MeV and at a density of 1/3 of normal nuclear density.
the multifragmentation of hot nuclei is a liquid-gas phase transition, and that the dynamics and thermodynamics are strongly correlated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics and the thermodynamics of the liquid-gas phase transition.
the dynamics of multifragmentation of hot nuclei and with the correlation of different signals indicative of the liquid-gas phase transition.
the dynamics and thermodynamics associated with the liquid-gas phase transition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phase transition is a well-established fact in heavy ion collisions at intermediate energy, with a liquid-gas type phase transition being a possible candidate.
a first order liquid-gas phase transition is observed in hot nuclei.
the experimental data are consistent with the existence of a liquid-gas phase transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a phase transition is observed in heavy systems and the liquid-gas phase transition is the most likely candidate.
the multifragmentation of hot nuclei is a signature of the phase transition from a compressed liquid to a gas of nucleons.
the experimental data show a clear evidence of a liquid-gas phase transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamical signals (fragment multiplicity and kinetic energies) are strongly correlated with the thermodynamical signals (temperature and pressure).
a correlation between dynamical signals, such as the kinetic energy of the light charged particles (LCPs), and thermodynamical ones, such as the excitation energy and the entropy, is observed.
the multifragmentation process is driven by a first-order phase transition in the system, and that this transition can be studied in a thermodynamic way.
